newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks show strong gains, brisk volume.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks show strong gains, brisk volume.

text.p: Argentine stocks slipped off their highs at the close Friday but still mustered strong gains helped by sound turnover, dealers said.
"The market has clearly regained the initiative thanks to a wave of buying on Wall Street and could tilt further to the upside," said analyst Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
The blue-chip MerVal index index jumped 2.1 percent to 532.26, boosting gains this week to 4.5 percent.
Floor volume surged to a five-week high of 26.7 million pesos, against 16 million Thursday and a recent daily average of 12 million.

"The sense we get here is that Wall Street is really driven by electoral factors, perhaps even more than by interest rates these days, and I think the bolsa is likely to remain conditioned by that trend," said Bonanno.
Locally, investors will remain anxious to see progress on tax and labor reforms, dealers said.
"Things are slowly getting better but for the markets the key word is 'slowly,' which means 'painful'," said a trader at a large emerging markets brokerage.
He said the government is trying to make up for a lack of economic leadership which has kept players guessing for weeks.

"(President Carlos) Menem's speech yesterday seemed aimed at recovering lost ground," said the trader, referring to a meeting of ruling Peronist Party leaders Thursday in which Menem made a resounding appeal for unity.
Technical analysts forecast the MerVal would rub up against resistance at 540 early next week and then pull back gently on profit-taking.

"We should also start to see more selective trading, with investors screening each sector carefully to see how tax hikes and other planned fiscal measures could hurt business and earnings," Bonanno said.
In the session the broad market outperformed the MerVal with a 2.4 percent gain. Winners thrashed losers 50 to 10 and 10 issues closed unchanged.
Over-the-counter deals picked up to 88.3 million pesos from 66.9 million Thursday.
Top MerVal gainers were construction stock Juan Minetti and Banco de Galicia, which charged up 5.1 percent and 4.8 percent, respectively.
Oil giant YPF, the market bellwether, grew a hefty 2.5 percent on news of a leadership change next April, while heavyweights Telefonica and Telecom both rallied 3.0 percent.

The only MerVal losers were foods giant Molinos, which shed 0.3 percent, and petrochemical concern Ipako, which stumbled 6.0 percent after surging 14 percent Thursday on news it was merging with second-tier holding company Garovaglio.

Garovaglio, which will absorb Ipako, rocketed 18.6 percent in the session after a 10 percent gain Thursday while Baesa, also a second-line stock, mimicked Thursday's action with a 10 percent rise driven by reports of a debt restructuring plan.
